title: How Big Tech Lies About AI Layoffs
description:
🚨 The "AI is taking our jobs" narrative is apparently a massive corporate cover-up.

Big companies aren’t laying off thousands of people because AI suddenly replaced them overnight. They’re laying people off because they over-hired and got WAY too bloated. 📉

Instead of CEOs admitting they made a massive management mistake (which looks terrible to investors), they’re saying "we're becoming more efficient with AI" instead and hoping it'll pump stock prices.

But it seems like investors have caught on. Companies using the "AI excuse" are actually seeing their stock prices drop nowadays.

What do you think? Are companies using AI to hide bad management, or is AI a real threat in your industry?

#AI #AInews #Layoffs #BusinessNews
transcript: Most of the layoffs we've seen, they're using AI as an excuse, but the reality is much different from what I can tell. A lot of these big companies that are laying tons and tons of people off, well, they were bloated companies. They were companies that did a ton of hiring during 2020, 2021, during COVID. They got way, way too big. Their expenses got way too high. Now they're realizing they could be much more profitable if they actually cut back. And instead of just saying we're cutting back to be more profitable because we don't want as much overhead, they're saying, "Oh, AI is doing a lot more of these jobs." They also believe this is positively going to impact their stock prices because if they say, "Hey, we're laying off a bunch of people because we got too bloated." Well, that doesn't look good for stockholders. But if they say, "Hey, we're laying a bunch of people off because AI is making this much more efficient." Well, stockholders now think they're geniuses. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is telling CEOs to stop hiding behind AI as the reason they're letting people go. He went on international television and called the AI layoff excuse lazy and irresponsible one week after DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis said the same thing in different words.

Love you Matt, but this feels a little too convenient.

Sure - some CEOs could be using AI as cover for layoffs they wanted to make anyway. Cooking COVID over hires happened. Margin pressure is real. But so is AI’s labor impact.
